$comment: Session boundary for the console (plan.md 15 and 11-25). What enforces the boundary is the commit gate, checks 35 and 41; this file states it, and only part of it is enforced at write time. Three groups, as in bridge/.claude/settings.json, and they do not all do the same amount.

permissions.$comment_1_reachable: THE FIRST EIGHT ENFORCE. A leading / anchors a path pattern at the session's primary working directory, which for a session started here is console/ (code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions, 'Read and Edit', as microscope_runtime/.claude/settings.json read it on 2026-10-17), while a bare pattern resolves against the current directory, which can move. So Edit(/tasks/**) means console/tasks/** and Edit(/README.md) means console/README.md alone. They were bare until 2026-10-17, and a bare filename matches at every depth, so Edit(README.md) would also have refused console/web/README.md and every fixture README, which are the console seat's own files: the over-match microscope_agent/.claude/settings.json records for plan.md. A pattern naming console/ itself would resolve inside it and guard nothing. All four paths are the manager's (seats.json, manager-console), and an execution session can reach all four; a seat that can edit its own orders has none. The Claude Code documentation says Write rules are never consulted and Edit covers writes, so each Write line is intent and its Edit twin is the rule. Not a constraint on the manager, whose session sits at the repository root and never loads this file.
permissions.$comment_2_command: THE COMMAND PATTERNS ENFORCE, against the text of a command and nothing else. The console's imported server can open a real Micro-Manager core (--backend mm-real with --mm-config) and pass light and motion operations to dino's own engine, which 11-25 rule 3 forbids; the live host lights the sample; the runtime's entry points are the instrument's. These lines stop a session typing them. They do not stop code that reaches the same place by another spelling, so they are a guard on a session, not on the code, and the code's own refusals are what the move must keep. None names a reading utility or contracts/, so check 53 passes them, but that is not the same as never blocking a read: a pattern matches the whole command text, so a Bash or PowerShell grep whose search word is one of these is refused too (the console seat met it on 2026-10-18, searching the lock). Read and search those words with the Read and Grep tools, which no command pattern reaches, and never reword a command to get past a denial. EACH HAS A PowerShell(...) TWIN, added 2026-10-17 after the console seat probed both shells from console/: `echo guard-probe mm-real` was denied through the Bash tool, and `Write-Output "guard-probe mm-real"` ran through the PowerShell tool, which is the Office computer's primary shell. After 950bff0c the same session ran the line again through PowerShell and was refused, with no restart between: the PowerShell(...) form is honoured, and these twins enforce as the Bash lines do.
permissions.$comment_2b_librarian: mcp__librarian DENIES EVERY TOOL OF THE LIBRARIAN'S SERVER. A console has no question, so it holds no caller_id, and a query that leaves a log line and no kb_refs on any card is what the card contract exists to prevent (console/CLAUDE.md). The rule was kept by hand until the console seat found the tools loaded in its session after it moved to console/. Not a read refusal in check 53's sense: the files under librarian_agent/ stay readable, and only the service is closed.
permissions.$comment_3_outward: THE REST ARE INTENT. They name the repository's other folders through the //**/soft-matter-agents/ form, which only a folder of that name can match; whether Claude Code honours the form is not documented, so count them as a statement of what this seat must not write, not as protection. Check 35 is what refuses such a commit.

hooks.command: sh -c 'for c in python3 python py; do command -v "$c" >/dev/null 2>&1 || continue; "$c" -c "" >/dev/null 2>&1 || continue; exec "$c" "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/contracts/validate.py" --quiet; done; echo "validate: no RUNNABLE python on PATH (python3, python, py all failed a -c probe)" >&2; exit 1'
hooks.$comment: The validator's exit code is the only truth (plan.md 8). Resolved from the git root, as bridge/'s is, so a session rooted at console/ finds it.

hooks.command: sh -c 'for c in python3 python py; do command -v "$c" >/dev/null 2>&1 || continue; "$c" -c "" >/dev/null 2>&1 || continue; exec "$c" "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/.claude/end-of-turn-commit-check.py"; done; exit 0'
hooks.$comment: The person's request, 2026-09-25: sessions commit and push what they made and learned before they stop. Asks once and never acts, as in every agent's settings.
